---
title: "Heterogeneous Kuramoto Network"
subtitle: "Three vertex types on a ring: standard, static, and inertia"
---

Replicates the full [NetworkDynamics.jl Heterogeneous System tutorial](https://juliadynamics.github.io/NetworkDynamics.jl/stable/generated/heterogeneous_system/) — an 8-node ring network with three different vertex types:

- **Kuramoto** (6 nodes): standard phase oscillator $\dot{\theta} = \omega_0 + \text{esum}$
- **StaticNode** (1 node): no dynamics, outputs a fixed phase parameter
- **KuramotoInertia** (1 node): second-order oscillator with angular velocity $\dot{\omega} = \omega_0 - \omega + \text{esum}$

Per-node parameter overrides set heterogeneous natural frequencies.

## YAML Specification

```{python}
#| echo: false
from IPython.display import Code, Markdown
Code(filename="yaml/heterogeneous_kuramoto.yaml", language="yaml")
```

## Model Report

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from tvbo import SimulationExperiment
exp = SimulationExperiment.from_file("yaml/heterogeneous_kuramoto.yaml")
Markdown(exp.generate_report())
```

## Generated Julia Code

```{python}
from tvbo import SimulationExperiment
exp = SimulationExperiment.from_file("yaml/heterogeneous_kuramoto.yaml")
Code(exp.render_code("networkdynamics"), language='julia')
```

## Run & Plot

```{python}
ts = exp.run(format="networkdynamics")
ts.plot()
```
